v.why: Replacing a 'none' on edge 0 reconnects node 1 and all of its downstream edges, so the gain exceeds that of swapping one live op for another.
With edge 0 removed, node 1 has no input, so a conv on edge 2 does nothing.
Node 2 output is never used when edge 5 is 'none', so conv on edge 1 is wasted.
With edge 5 removed, the skip on edge 3 is a key gradient path and its marginal value rises.
A strong conv path on edge 5 already supplies the output signal, so the direct skip on edge 3 adds less.
Capacity at the output node saturates when edge 4 already carries a 3x3 conv.
A second 3x3 conv into node 3 has diminishing returns when edge 5 is already one.
Feature extraction from the input saturates when edge 0 is already a 3x3 conv.
Deleting the identity shortcut hurts more than deleting other ops on that edge because it is a key gradient path.
Replacing a parameter-free pool with a learnable conv gains more than replacing an existing 3x3 conv.
